summary.text: Nylon is a family of synthetic polymers characterized by amide linkages.
As thermoplastics, nylons can be melt-processed into fibers, films and diverse shapes.
Nylon was the first commercially successful synthetic thermoplastic polymer, and Wallace Hume Carothers made the first one at DuPont.

facts.label: Nylon 6
facts.value: Developed by Paul Schlack at IG Farben in 1938

facts.label: First year sales
facts.value: 64 million pairs of stockings sold in 1940

facts.label: Wartime use
facts.value: Almost all production went to parachutes and cord

items.prompt: A nylon is named nylon-6,6, with two numbers. What does that name point to?

options.label: It is made from a single aminocarboxylic acid
It is made from six repeat units of caprolactam
It is made from a diamine and a dicarboxylic acid of set chain lengths
It is made from two copies of the same monomer

items.explain: The nylon-XY family is derived from diamines and dicarboxylic acids with carbon chain lengths X and Y.

items.prompt: During World War II, where did almost all nylon production go?

options.label: To the military, for parachutes and parachute cord
To women's stockings sold in department stores
To toothbrush bristles for soldiers
To the 1939 New York World's Fair

items.explain: Almost all nylon production was diverted to the military for use in parachutes and parachute cord.

items.prompt: Why did DuPont's nylon project need its Ammonia Department?

options.label: The department supplied the rayon fibers it was built on
Some key ingredients had to be made using high pressure chemistry
The department ran the 1939 World's Fair display
The department owned the patent for the polymer

items.explain: Some of the key ingredients had to be produced using high pressure chemistry, the Ammonia Department's main area of expertise.

items.prompt: After early successes in 1930, how did the direction of Carothers' team change?

options.label: From industrial work back to purely theoretical research
From polymers to a sole focus on cellulose-based fibers
From the laboratory to designing and running a chemical plant
From general polymerization research to one combination for industry

items.explain: After those discoveries, the team shifted from investigating general polymerization toward a practical goal of finding one chemical combination for industrial applications.

items.prompt: Nylon is a thermoplastic. What does that let manufacturers do with it?

options.label: Melt-process it into fibers, films and other shapes
Cure it into one fixed shape that cannot be melted again
Spin it only into fibers and never into films
Shape it only while it is cold

items.explain: As thermoplastics, nylons can be melt-processed into fibers, films and diverse shapes.

items.prompt: Which earlier technique did Carothers use in 1935 to fully develop nylon?

options.label: The rayon process DuPont had used on cellulose fibers
The high pressure method of the Ammonia Department
The cold drawing method that coworker Julian Hill used for a polyester in 1930
The caprolactam route that Paul Schlack developed

items.explain: Julian W. Hill used a cold drawing method to produce a polyester in 1930, and Carothers later used it in 1935 to fully develop nylon.
